criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both use an elevated oblique view with upright vertical structures and diagonal ground axes.
Both frame a complete industrial district rather than a close-up landmark.
different: REFERENCE has a shallower, landscape-led valley view; CANDIDATE is more top-down and tile-plane dominant.
REFERENCE frames broad terrain depth, while CANDIDATE is tighter around buildings and route infrastructure.

evidence.observation: Broad oblique valley framing with receding mountains and city at the right edge.
Higher, flatter isometric framing centered on the developed tile plane.
Large mountain and open-valley foreground establishes shallow scenic depth.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both concentrate dense town blocks beside heavy industrial facilities.
Both retain rocky or undeveloped margins around the occupied district.
different: REFERENCE preserves a broad open central valley; CANDIDATE fills much more of the center and upper map with repeated buildings.
CANDIDATE distributes several large plant compounds across the map, while REFERENCE concentrates its main industrial mass near the bottom.

evidence.observation: Open valley separates the right-side city from the concentrated lower industrial district.
Town blocks and industrial compounds occupy most of the central playable area.
Primary dense industrial mass is concentrated along the lower corridor.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both show a dark blue-gray sinuous channel cut through industrial terrain.
In both, infrastructure bridges the channel and facilities sit close to its banks.
different: REFERENCE uses a narrower, mostly vertical valley channel; CANDIDATE uses a wider diagonal channel with different bends.
CANDIDATE has two prominent orange-deck bridges and flatter water, versus one dominant bridge and softer reflective water in REFERENCE.

evidence.observation: Narrow channel descends through a deep shaded valley with muted reflections.
Wider dark channel runs diagonally across the tiled district.
One dominant bridge attaches the lower industrial banks.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Major plants dominate nearby houses, while pylons remain intermediate-scale landmarks.
Bridges and utility structures are readable individually in both maps.
different: CANDIDATE plants, bridges, and pylons occupy substantially more screen area relative to town blocks.
REFERENCE has compact nuclear-site silhouettes and a prominent lower substation; CANDIDATE emphasizes large thermal plants without an equally dominant substation form.

evidence.observation: Two compact nuclear-site silhouettes remain small against the landscape.
Large industrial complex and cyan substation establish a layered landmark scale.
Thermal plant compounds and bridges are large relative to surrounding blocks.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both combine blackened metal, dark concrete and soil with sparse amber illumination.
Both maintain dense industrial surface detail across structures, terrain, and chrome framing.
different: REFERENCE has warmer sepia midtones and atmospheric painterly blending.
CANDIDATE is nearer-black, sharper, and more visibly repetitive at the tile and sprite level.

evidence.observation: Warm charcoal terrain, smoky midtones, and amber highlights form a cohesive industrial palette.
Matching charcoal-and-amber palette rendered with crisper, darker tiled textures.
Industrial structures blend concrete, soot, metal, and warm window light.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both clearly separate energized cyan conductors from planned amber routes.
Both use multi-strand conductors attached to repeated transmission towers with readable sag.
different: REFERENCE routes cyan around the lower perimeter and amber from two siting options; CANDIDATE forms a large cyan loop with shorter dashed amber branches.
CANDIDATE cyan strokes are brighter and more ribbon-like, while REFERENCE conductors integrate more softly with the terrain.

evidence.observation: Cyan energized conductors track a lower tower corridor and converge near the substation.
Bright cyan multi-line loop attaches to pylons around the central district.
Amber paired conductors visibly connect both candidate sites toward the grid.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both use riveted industrial chrome with a segmented top bar, left tool kit, and right inspector.
Both organize inspector choices with amber and cyan accents over a dark map-integrated frame.
different: REFERENCE gives larger numeric cost hierarchy and fills the inspector vertically; CANDIDATE uses smaller text and leaves a large empty lower inspector area.
CANDIDATE top chrome is more heavily segmented and ornamented than the slimmer REFERENCE status strip.

evidence.observation: Slim riveted top status strip uses large centered readouts.
Taller segmented top bar uses matching dark metal and amber/cyan accents.
Right inspector is filled by two large comparison cards and prominent action buttons.
